goal: Adopt a single test framework for pricing-service that keeps the existing suite running in CI and stays maintainable going forward.
question: Which test framework should pricing-service standardize on going forward, given its existing pytest-based one-file suite, its CI workflow, and its zero-runtime-dependency packaging?
known_constraints: CI must keep running the test suite on every push in the existing GitHub Actions workflow.
The test framework must be installable through the dev extra, because CI runs `pip install -e .[dev]` before testing.
README and onboarding documentation currently assume pytest, so any non-pytest choice requires documentation updates.

environment.repo_layout: src layout (src/pricing) with tests in tests/
environment.ci: GitHub Actions workflow 'ci' on push: pip install -e .[dev], then pytest
environment.current_framework: pytest>=8 declared as a dev optional dependency

evidence: pyproject.toml declares dev optional-dependency pytest>=8 while the project has zero runtime dependencies (pyproject.toml).
The existing suite is a single file, tests/test_pricing.py, written with pytest idioms: `import pytest`, @pytest.mark.parametrize, and plain assert statements (tests/test_pricing.py).
README states: 'All tests run under pytest in CI; the suite and onboarding docs assume pytest.' (README.md)
CI installs the package with its dev extra and runs pytest as the only test step (github/workflows/ci.yml).
No unittest usage, no [tool.pytest.ini_options] configuration, and no other test tooling exists anywhere in the repository (repository scan).
The package under test is a small pure-function service: src/pricing/__init__.py defines a single function tier_price(seats) (src/pricing/__init__.py).

alternatives.name: Keep pytest (status quo)
alternatives.description: Continue using pytest>=8 as the project's test framework with no change to dependencies, tests, or CI.
advantages: The existing test file runs unchanged; it already uses @pytest.mark.parametrize and plain asserts.
CI and the dev extra already install and invoke pytest, so there is no migration work.
README and onboarding docs already assume pytest, so no documentation update is needed.
disadvantages: Keeps a third-party dev dependency for a package that otherwise has zero dependencies.
Framework upgrades must be tracked across future pytest major versions.
assumptions: pytest>=8 remains actively maintained on Python >= 3.10.
The team is not required to adopt a stdlib-only testing policy.

alternatives.name: Migrate to stdlib unittest
alternatives.description: Replace pytest with the Python standard library unittest module and drop the pytest dev dependency.
advantages: Removes the only third-party dev dependency, since unittest ships with Python >= 3.10.
No upstream framework upgrades to track; the stdlib lifecycle follows the Python version in use.
disadvantages: The existing test must be rewritten from @pytest.mark.parametrize to unittest.TestCase methods or subTest.
CI needs a new runner invocation and README's statement that the suite assumes pytest becomes false, so docs must change.
assumptions: The one-file suite will not grow to need pytest fixtures or plugins.
The team accepts TestCase-style assertion methods instead of plain assert statements.

alternatives.name: Keep pytest plus curated plugin stack
alternatives.description: Keep pytest>=8 and standardize going forward by adding a curated plugin set, for example pytest-cov and pytest-xdist, to the dev extra and CI.
advantages: The existing test file, CI invocation, and README all keep working because plugins are additive.
Adds coverage reporting and parallel execution ahead of any suite growth.
disadvantages: Grows the dev dependency list and adds plugin-version compatibility constraints on top of pytest.
Coverage and parallelism are not required by anything currently visible in the repository.
assumptions: The suite is expected to grow enough that coverage and parallel runs pay off.
Plugin release cadence stays compatible with pytest>=8.

criteria.name: Existing suite compatibility
rubric: Requires a full rewrite of the existing suite
Requires a partial rewrite of the existing suite

criteria.name: CI and documentation integration
rubric: Requires rewriting CI and updating docs
Requires minor CI or doc adjustment
No CI or doc change needed

rubric: High burden: stagnant or deprecated tooling
Moderate burden: periodic third-party updates to track
Low burden: stable and actively maintained or stdlib-provided

rubric: Keeps or adds a single dev dependency
